findings.title: SupportCandy AI Customer Support plugin XSS and SQL injection cluster
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-94378 reports authenticated stored cross-site scripting in the SupportCandy - AI Customer Support Ticket System & Live Chatbot Agent WordPress plugin through 3.5.3 via the name parameter. CVE-2026-94539 reports authenticated time-based SQL injection in the same plugin through 3.5.3 via the sort_by parameter, requiring a WordPress subscriber-level role and a SupportCandy Agent account with Assign Agents permission.
findings.evidence_classification: Primary CVE records with CNA-provided Wordfence references and WordPress plugin source-change references.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SupportCandy - AI Customer Support Ticket System & Live Chatbot Agent <= 3.5.3; customer/agent ticket fields and ticket sorting query paths.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is an AI customer-support and live-chatbot plugin, so the affected boundary can sit inside customer-support workflows where agent-facing ticket data, user identities, and helpdesk actions are exposed to lower-privileged accounts. The SQL injection record also has a data-confidentiality impact in a support system likely to hold sensitive customer context.
named_entities: AI Customer Support Ticket System & Live Chatbot Agent

findings.title: WPZOOM Connect AI Chat sensitive information exposure
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-100149 reports that WPZOOM Connect: AI Chat, Click to Chat, Social Icons & Share Buttons through 4.7.3 exposes sensitive customer information through an HMAC signature domain-separation flaw in the AI chat customer endpoint. An unauthenticated attacker can extract a customer card for an arbitrary victim email address, including name, WordPress user ID, order history, order totals, purchased products, payment method labels, and EDD Software Licensing license keys with status and activation counts.
findings.evidence_classification: Primary CVE record with CNA-provided Wordfence, WordPress source, and GitHub commit references.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: WPZOOM Connect: AI Chat, Click to Chat, Social Icons & Share Buttons <= 4.7.3; AI chat customer data endpoint and HMAC signature verification.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The affected product is an AI chat integration that bridges site visitor identity, commerce records, and customer support context. The flaw turns chat/customer integration state into a data-exposure boundary and can disclose license keys and commerce history without authentication.

findings.title: Alt Text AI post content authorization bypass
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-91108 reports a missing authorization flaw in Alt Text AI through 1.10.41. Authenticated subscriber-level users can obtain a nonce from admin pages and invoke an AJAX action that overwrites the post_content of any post or page, including content they do not own, with LLM-generated text influenced by attacker-controlled keywords; the record also notes unauthorized consumption of the site owner's paid AltText.ai API credits.
findings.evidence_classification: Primary CVE record with CNA-provided Wordfence and WordPress plugin source references.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Alt Text AI <= 1.10.41; atai_enrich_post_content AJAX action, nonce exposure, post content modification, and paid AltText.ai API usage.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is an AI-generated-content control failure: a low-privilege user can trigger model-backed content generation against content they do not own, causing unauthorized content mutation and consumption of paid AI service credits.
